notes: v10.4 BUILD REFRESH (2026-11-24, b4822 — the twenty-third cut — small words are never glued into a word you never use; a name you correct three times is learned, notarized): (1) Small words are never glued into a word you never use. Words said in one breath are joined into one longer word only when that word is yours: your History holds it, or you named it as the right word in a report. "In broad daylight" stays "in broad daylight"; it is no longer written "inboard daylight". On our 3,000-recording check this repair corrects 20 recordings and breaks none. (2) A name you correct by hand three times is learned. This now holds for a short name of three letters, for a name of two words, and for the possessive of a name. The corrections are read in any app, and a correction typed letter by letter is counted once, when you finish it. (3) A spelling you taught is never overwritten by a loose Dictionary match. An entry's exact spoken form still wins; only the near-miss match stands down on a w
